text.p: Apple Computer Inc. reported a second-quarter loss of $708 million Wednesday, reflecting one-time charges and weaker sales by the troubled computer maker.

Apple said the loss for the quarter ended March 28, which equaled $5.64 a share, compared with a loss of $740 million, or $5.99 a share, in the year-ago quarter, when Apple was also hit by one-time charges. Revenues fell to $1.6 billion in the latest quarter from $2.19 billion in last year's quarter.
Apple, which pioneered the personal computer, has struggled in recent years from missed opportunities, management turmoil and failed stratagies.

Over the last three years, the Cupertino, Calif.-based company has laid off thousands of workers and replaced most of its senior management. It fired former Chief Executive Michael Spindler, replacing him with outside board member Gilbert Amelio, and also hired back its two founders -- Steven Jobs and Stephen Wozniak -- to advise Amelio.

Aside from its other problems, Apple has been hurt by higher costs than its rivals because it needs to support both the hardware and software sides of its business. Other companies, such as software giant Microsoft Corp., can devote all of their financial resources to improving their software, while rival PC makers such as Compaq and Dell focus on the hardware.
